Consent and DPDP: notice, purpose and the consent ledger

After this lesson you can:
  • Explain purpose-bound consent and the DPDP notice
  • Describe withdrawal, correction and erasure — and the statutory-retention tension
  • Show where consent gates the LoanOS application flow

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Consent is a contract about data
  2. The ledger, not the checkbox
  3. Digital lending adds its own data rules
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Consent is a contract about data

The DPDP Act makes personal-data processing lawful only with a valid basis — for lending, overwhelmingly notice and consent.

A valid consent is specific: it names the purpose (credit assessment, bureau pull, marketing), the data involved, and the recipients.

Blanket 'we may use your data for anything' consent is exactly what the regime forbids.

The borrower also holds rights: access to what is held, correction of what is wrong, erasure of what is no longer needed, and a grievance path. Each right is a workflow, not a sentiment.

2. The ledger, not the checkbox

LoanOS records consent in a consent ledger: purpose-specific entries with notice evidence, grant/withdrawal status and timestamps.

The application preflight reads the ledger — an application without current, purpose-matched consent fails closed.

Withdrawal propagates: a revoked marketing consent must stop campaigns, and a revoked processing consent routes the case to a governed exception, because a live loan cannot simply forget its borrower.

That is the tension a BA must internalise: DPDP rights meet statutory retention. KYC records and transaction history carry mandatory retention periods under PMLA/RBI rules; an erasure request is honoured by erasing what can be erased and placing a documented statutory hold on what cannot — with the reason disclosed to the borrower.

3. Digital lending adds its own data rules

The Digital Lending Directions layer lending-specific duties on top of DPDP: data collection by DLAs must be need-based, with borrower consent; no access to phone contacts, media or other invasive scopes; personal data stays on India servers (if processed abroad, it is deleted there and returned within 24 hours). Purpose limitation is enforced at the integration boundary — a document collected for KYC does not silently become a marketing asset.

Regulatory anchors

  • DPDP-2023 — Lawful purpose, notice/consent, principal rights, breach duties.
  • DPDP-RULES-2025 — Operational notice/consent and breach-notification detail under a phased commencement schedule.
  • RBI-DATA-RESIDENCY — Digital-lending personal data stays in India; 24-hour return rule for offshore processing.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability CON-001 — Purpose-specific notice and consent ledger.
  • Capability CON-003 — Consent denial, withdrawal and downstream propagation.
  • Capability CON-008 — Erasure request with statutory-retention hold.
  • Code packages/core/src/compliance/compliance-controls.js — Consent and DPDP notice evidence checks in the application preflight.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. A borrower with a live loan demands full erasure. The correct outcome is:

  1. Erase everything immediately
  2. Refuse — borrowers cannot ask
  3. Erase what is erasable and place a documented statutory hold on retained records, informing the borrower
  4. Close the loan first
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. DPDP rights operate alongside PMLA/RBI retention duties; the platform models this as erasure-with-hold, never silent refusal.

2. What makes a consent entry usable by the application preflight?

  1. Any signed T&C
  2. Purpose-matched, currently granted, with notice evidence
  3. A verbal confirmation noted by staff
  4. The KYC record
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Consent is purpose-specific and time-variant; the preflight checks the ledger for a current grant matching the processing purpose.
